- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is above recent lows, adjust downward by 1–2% to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.3–0.7) and forecast shows strong trend, apply a 3–5 day lag correction to avoid premature peaks.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, reweight forecast toward recent 7-day average to reduce horizon bias.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.1–0.3) and forecast is rising, suppress upward momentum until sentiment stabilizes above 0.4.
